chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from one of his companions, from Aban, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who is claimed against for a right, and there is no proof for the owner of the right: He said: The defendant is sworn an oath. So if he refuses to swear and says, 'I turn the oath upon you,' to the owner of the right, then that is obligatory upon the owner of the right that he swears and takes his wealth.

key_terms.أَرُدُّ الْيَمِينَ عَلَيْكَ: I turn the oath upon you

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a plaintiff has no proof and the defendant refuses to swear an oath?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the mechanism of 'iradat al-yamin' (turning the oath), a key principle in Shia jurisprudence where the burden of proof shifts when the defendant refuses to swear. It highlights the defendant's right to compel the plaintiff to take an oath to secure their claim, reflecting the practical application of evidentiary rules in the absence of written documentation. This procedure underscores the flexibility of Shia legal theory in balancing rights when clear evidence is lacking.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from one of his companions, from Aban, from a man,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who is claimed against (defendant) for the right, and there is no proof for the owner of the right. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The defendant would swear an oath. So if he refuses to swear and says, ‘I turn the swearing of the oath upon you’, to the owner of the right, so that would be obligatory upon the owner of the right that he swears, and takes his wealth’.
en.sarwar: 4. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah, from certain persons of his people from Aban from a man who has narrated the following: “This is about the case of a man who claims to have a right on another man but does not have any testimony. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘He can ask the defendant to take an oath, but if he declines and asks the plaintiff to take an oath, then it is obligatory on him to take an oath to receive his right.’”
